ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Primary text, deepest foreground — the absolute ink for body copy and legal/footer type

zinc-ink.$description: Zinc Ink — Headlines, nav text, icons, filled button background — the universal interactive ink

slate-700.$description: Slate 700 — Body text emphasis, input fill backgrounds for dark/inverted inputs

slate-600.$description: Slate 600 — Secondary body text, input borders, subtle button borders

slate-500.$description: Slate 500 — Muted helper text, link text, icon details

zinc-500.$description: Zinc 500 — Icon strokes (the dominant icon color), secondary UI lines

zinc-300.$description: Zinc 300 — Card borders when slightly more definition is needed than the default hairline

zinc-200.$description: Zinc 200 — Universal hairline border — by far the most-used color in the system at 360+ border applications

zinc-100.$description: Zinc 100 — Card surfaces, hero background tint, subtle section backgrounds

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page-tinted background variant, near-white surfaces for cards that need separation from pure white

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Primary canvas and card surface — the page sits on white

footer-green.$description: Footer Green — Footer band background — the only chromatic UI color, a friendly grass green that punctuates the monochrome page

gelica.$description: Display and heading face — a custom chunky serif used exclusively for h1/h2 moments. Tight line-heights (1.0–1.11) make stacked headlines feel dense and editorial. Normal letter-spacing.

articulat-cf.$description: Body, UI, and small-label face. The defining quirk: 0.28em letter-spacing on this family creates the system's signature airy, architectural feel — almost certainly applied to small/uppercase labels and meta text where the wide tracking reads as deliberate typesetting rather than gap. Generous line-heights (up to 1.78) keep body copy breathing.
